subject: Day 12: maternal lochia tapering; growth spurt prep
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 12. End of week 2 approaches. The first growth spurt is coming in the next 2-9 days (days 14-21); expect 24-48 hours of cluster feeding then a reset. Maternal lochia is in the alba stage — yellowish-white, minimal. Most of the week-1 worries are behind you.

Action items
- Stock up on staple foods that one parent can eat one-handed: dense calorie bars, hummus and pita, hard-boiled eggs, peanut butter. The growth spurt will eat the mother's reserves if breastfeeding.
- Confirm the 1-month well visit is on the calendar (target day 28-35). AAP Bright Futures periodicity schedule: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Drop a thank-you to the lactation consultant, doula, or anyone else who supported the first week. A short voice note works better than a card; these professionals share referrals based on memorable patients.
- Take a 20-minute walk together if the mother feels up to it. Light walking is approved for most uncomplicated vaginal deliveries by week 2. Cesarean recovery follows a different timeline — defer to the OB. ACOG postpartum care overview: https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/postpartum-pain-management
- Continue the feeding log.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Cord stump likely detached. Mother's bleeding minimal and yellow-white. Cluster feeding 60-90 minutes most evenings.
- [low concern] Avi sleeping in 60-90 minute increments at night.
- [monitor] Persistent baby blues in the mother (tearfulness, anxiety, sleep disruption beyond what Avi imposes). 50-80% of mothers experience baby blues; resolution by week 2 is typical. Persistence beyond week 2 escalates concern toward postpartum depression. CDC overview of postpartum depression: https://www.cdc.gov/reproductive-health/depression/index.html
- [call within 24h] Yellow tinge still spreading. Persistent inability to latch. Fewer than six wet diapers per day. Mother's bleeding suddenly heavier or saturated pads.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusal of all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Mother chest pain, severe headache, or vision changes — call OB or 911. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunity
Tummy time during awake-alert windows accumulating 10-15 minutes total today. Use a rolled receiving blanket under his chest if he fatigues quickly. AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 14-21: first common growth spurt; expect 24-48 hours of feeding-frequency uptick.
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit window opens; first social smiles begin.
- Day 35-42: peak of the PURPLE crying curve at about 6 weeks.
- Day 42: maternal 6-week postpartum visit.

Further reading
- ACOG on the postpartum period (week 1-6): https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/postpartum-pain-management
- CDC overview of postpartum depression: https://www.cdc.gov/reproductive-health/depression/index.html
- AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Cribsheet by Emily Oster: https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/562146/cribsheet-by-emily-oster/
